HOW IT WORKS

From maker claim
to evidence you can read.

We are building a marketplace where each listed product has a maker story, a source trail and an honest account of what has and has not been checked.

THE PLANNED JOURNEY

Verify. List. Buy. Review.

Each stage has a clear gate. We are preparing the verification and listing process before opening purchases.

  1. 01 / VERIFY

    Research the maker

    Check public identity, years trading, audit badges, documents and possible red flags. A person reviews the report.

  2. 02 / LIST

    Show the evidence

    Publish approved products with their specifications, origin story, early FI Score and links to sources.

  3. 03 / BUY

    Make an informed choice

    Product availability, delivered cost and payment terms must be confirmed before online ordering opens.

  4. 04 / REVIEW

    Keep learning

    Buyer feedback can become another signal after real purchases. No customer-review data exists yet.

FI VERIFY

What we check.

FI Verify starts with a maker’s name, website and product page. Each approved product shows what we checked, the date we checked it and links to the sources. Its FI Score is an early score, based on our research, and it can change as more checks are completed.

We use public pages only, one page at a time. We never log in to a site, get past a bot check or scrape in bulk.

  • IdentityDoes public information connect the maker to the business and website claimed?
  • Trading historyWhat can public records support about years in business?
  • Marketplace audit badgesWhat badge is shown, who issued it and what does it actually cover?
  • Documents and testsWhat certificates or reports are available, current and independently checkable?
  • Red flagsWhat visible inconsistencies or concerns need a buyer’s attention?

HOW WE RANK

An early score, with its evidence visible.

The FI Score is a research summary. It is not a certificate, a product performance guarantee or a substitute for checking suitability for your project.

15% OF FULL RUBRIC

Buyer experience

Verified buyer reviews when available. Until then, this reads “No reviews yet” and adds no points.

How missing evidence is handled. “Not stated” means the maker’s page doesn’t say. It is not a failed check, but it earns no points. A claimed certificate earns a few points until we check it on the issuer’s register, a verified one earns more, and a failed check takes points away. Until a product has buyer reviews, its score is an early score, based on our research.

CERTIFICATE CHECKS

A document is a claim until its source is checked.

For each certificate, we record its name, and its number and issuer where the maker states them. Its status is one of four: Verified, Claimed (not yet checked), Failed our check or Not stated.

  • Public registerWhere a register exists, we record the result and its link. Examples include IAF CertSearch for ISO certificates and the ABCB WaterMark database for relevant products.
  • Human decisionOnly a person can mark a certificate Verified after checking the issuer’s register. Test reports also need the laboratory’s accreditation checked.
  • Clear limitsIf a claim can’t be matched on the issuer’s register, it shows as Failed our check. A claim without a number stays Claimed until the maker sends one.

Every product needs a person’s approval before it appears. A public source or an AI-assisted draft alone never approves a maker.
